solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: 5 in malice hail corrupt political 29 (11)

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled and rearranged

annotation.surface: Something numbered five, hailed with malice, stands in a line about a corrupt political thinker.
annotation.walkthrough: The '5' is not a cross-reference to 5 Down but the Roman numeral V, which joins the anagram. 29 is PHILOSOPHER, so the definition reads 'political philosopher'.
annotation.definitionFit: Niccolò Machiavelli, author of The Prince, is the classic political philosopher.

entries.clue: Optimism at Chevening masks conflict (8)

indicators.note: the phrase covers the answer, which sits concealed inside it

annotation.surface: Cheerful talk at a diplomatic residence papers over a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: Chevening is the British Foreign Secretary's official country house, which makes the diplomatic scene plausible.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as a noun: two things that clash are said to be in conflict.

entries.clue: Black stray in Galilean location and city (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so B and ERR sit within the Galilean place

blocks.note: the Galilee village of the wedding feast in John's Gospel
to wander from the right path

annotation.surface: A dark stray animal wanders in a biblical spot and then a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black stray' reads as a dog or cat, but the two words split into separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Australian capital is one city among many.

entries.clue: Laity all over the place in Catholic country (5)

indicators.note: the letters are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: Lay churchgoers are scattered across a Catholic nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The laity are the non-clergy members of a church, which ties the fodder neatly to the Catholic setting.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: home of the Vatican, it is a largely Catholic nation.

entries.clue: Those watching six large water vessels (7)

annotation.surface: An audience keeps an eye on half a dozen big jugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Water vessels' suggests boats, but these are jugs.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a television audience is made up of people who watch.

entries.clue: Crime racket here and there in two American cities (7)

indicators.note: take letters from scattered spots: every other one
'in' places one thing inside another, so the racket's letters sit between the two cities

annotation.surface: A criminal racket operates in two US cities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racket' in the surface is organised crime, which sits well beside the definition, but here it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: theft is one particular crime, and this is its legal name.

entries.clue: Hindrance in Spain interrupting La Diablada? (9)

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, as E breaks into IMP DANCE

blocks.note: La Diablada is a dance of devils, so an imp dance

annotation.surface: Something gets in the way of a Spanish-speaking folk festival.
annotation.walkthrough: La Diablada is an Andean festival dance of masked devils; the question mark flags that 'imp dance' is a playful description of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: anything that impedes is a hindrance, and in electronics the word names resistance to current.

entries.clue: Fruit — predatory bird wanting kilo (3)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the bird is short of its K

blocks.note: K is kilo in the phonetic alphabet; it is removed

annotation.surface: A hawk, minus a kilo, is described as fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' in the surface could be hungry, fitting a predator, but it means without.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the red berry of the hawthorn is one kind of fruit.

entries.clue: Secret plan Häagen-Dazs suggests? (6,6)

blocks.note: a straight definition of a concealed scheme
the surface points to an ice-cream brand; the setter means the letters of the name, which conceal a six-letter word for a plan

annotation.surface: An ice-cream brand hints at a secret scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the brand as a crossword clue would: AGENDA is literally hidden inside HäAGEN-DAzs, so the name contains a hidden agenda.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: an ulterior motive kept out of sight is a concealed programme, a secret plan.

entries.clue: Hot stuff , did you see me hugging sailor? (6)

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms around someone, so WAS I wraps around AB

blocks.note: the question 'Was I?', as in was I seen

annotation.surface: Someone asks if they were spotted cuddling a sailor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests something sexy, which the hugging surface plays on, but it is spicy food.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the fiery green Japanese paste is one kind of hot stuff.

entries.clue: Motorsport icon Boleyn and Cleves recalled? (5)

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Anne Boleyn and Anne of Cleves, two of Henry VIII's wives

annotation.surface: A racing legend brings to mind two of Henry VIII's queens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' seems to mean remembered, as of history, but it asks for the letters to come back the other way.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Ayrton, the Brazilian triple Formula One champion, is a motorsport icon.

entries.clue: Dramatist in Eire is with DUP surprisingly (9)

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: A playwright in Ireland is unexpectedly in league with the DUP.
annotation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, so a dramatist in Eire siding with it would be surprising.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the three great Athenian tragedians is a dramatist.

entries.clue: Celt with an eye out for C2H2 (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: A Celt keeps a lookout for a chemical formula.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With an eye out for' reads as watching for something; 'out' is really the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Chemical formula: two carbons and two hydrogens make the welding gas.

entries.clue: Nerd one Royal Society girl embraces (5)

indicators.note: an embrace holds someone within the arms, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: the royal 'we', a monarch's word for oneself

annotation.surface: A geek is hugged by a debutante from the Royal Society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Royal Society' looks like the scientific academy, which suits a nerd, but the phrase must be split across two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, American slang for a socially awkward swot.

entries.clue: Say red and white containers? (7)

blocks.note: the surface suggests colours, as of a flag or a football strip
the setter means vessels for red and white wine, 'say' marking an example

annotation.surface: A question about vessels painted in red and white.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the definition is oblique: the containers hold wine rather than being coloured.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: glass flasks used to serve house wines of either colour.

entries.clue: Identify suspect advice in digital feature (9)

blocks.note: slang: to point the finger at a culprit

annotation.surface: Advice on picking out a suspect via some digital technology.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digital' is not about computers: digits are fingers.
annotation.definitionFit: Pun on 'digital': the end of a digit is a feature of it.

entries.clue: New Englander’s tooth extraction technique? (4)

blocks.note: short for Yankee, a word first used of people from the north-eastern US states

annotation.surface: A dentist from Massachusetts has a signature way of pulling teeth.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as 'is', joining the two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for an American, originally a northeasterner, and a sharp tug.

entries.clue: Stock pirate feature (archetype possibly not right) (8)

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged otherwise
'not' negates, so R is taken out of the fodder

annotation.surface: A stereotypical pirate's trademark is described as an archetype, maybe not quite right.
annotation.walkthrough: The parenthesis reads as a comment on the definition, but it is the whole of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the cliché one-eyed buccaneer wears one over the missing eye.

entries.clue: Cockney perhaps briefly sustained by kebab (8)

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: LONG, as in a sustained note, with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A Cockney, keeping going for a while on a kebab.
annotation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Ender, so 'perhaps' flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Cockneys are one kind of resident of the British capital.

entries.clue: U-boat carrying any number turned up (4)

indicators.note: a vessel carrying cargo holds it inside, so SUB holds N

blocks.note: N is the algebraic symbol for any number

annotation.surface: A German submarine with an unknown number aboard surfaced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is the definition: a snub nose is turned up at the tip.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: a short nose tilted at the end is described this way.

entries.clue: Rice dish one with no meat served up (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent upwards, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A rice dish is dished up by someone who adds no meat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Served up' fits the food surface; in a down clue it means read from the bottom upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a spiced South Asian dish is one based on rice.

entries.clue: Earl with most suitable temper receiving love now and then (5,2,5)

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the temper word takes O inside

blocks.note: as in 'the very thing', exactly right

annotation.surface: An aristocrat with the ideal temperament mellows, receiving love from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temper' reads as a noun, a mood, but it is the verb meaning to tone down.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: both phrases mean occasionally.

entries.clue: Composer leaving area green for painter (2,5)

indicators.note: the composer is leaving, that is going away from, the area, so A departs

annotation.surface: A composer quits the environmental patch to make way for an artist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Area green' reads as a village green, but the two words have separate jobs.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Cretan-born master of Renaissance Toledo is a painter.

entries.clue: See 7
Ailment endless with a river animal (6)

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

annotation.surface: A sick creature by a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ailment endless' suggests a chronic illness, but it asks for a word to be trimmed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the puma, or mountain lion, is one animal.

entries.clue: Maxim the Obscure Financier (5)

blocks.note: a faceless Swiss banker, in a famous British political jibe

annotation.surface: Reads like the title of a novel or film about a mysterious moneyman.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' was Harold Wilson's era phrase for secretive Swiss bankers.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a rare word for an aphorism, and a disparaging term for a shadowy banker.

entries.clue: Ginger fed with fish almost rallied (9)

indicators.note: something fed with food takes it inside, so the colour takes the fish in
the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: GROUPER, a sea fish, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A ginger cat, fed some fish, nearly recovered its spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like the spice or a cat, but it is a hair colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: troops that gather again after a setback have rallied.

entries.clue: Architectural feature in Kosovo lovely (5)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the phrase

annotation.surface: Praise for a building detail in a Balkan country.
annotation.walkthrough: This is an obscure term, so the hidden word is the way in; crossers help confirm it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a rounded convex moulding in classical building.

entries.clue: Horse chasing man discussed bad experience (9)

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is heard not seen
coming after, so MARE follows

blocks.note: a knight is a chess man

annotation.surface: A horse pursuing someone who was being talked about had a rough time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, and the knight is the one shaped like a horse, which ties the surface together.
annotation.definitionFit: Extended sense: a bad dream, and by extension any ordeal.

entries.clue: See 20
Simple tune not bad sans introduction (3)

indicators.note: sans is French for without, so the word loses its introduction, the opening letter

annotation.surface: A plain melody that is passable apart from its opening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not bad' is a single idea, passable, not a negation to act on.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a song or melody, as in Bach's Air on the G String.

entries.clue: Polish hero damaged absorbing pressure one thinks (11)

definitions.note: the definition is a clause, 'one [who] thinks', standing for the noun

indicators.note: the letters are broken and remade
to absorb is to soak something in, so P is taken into the mix of letters

annotation.surface: A wounded Polish hero, under strain, ponders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as a nationality, but it is plain anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a professional thinker, one whose trade is thought.
